before.evidence: A GROWABLE BUFFER HEADER embedded at RenderResourceEntry +0x10, declared 2026-09-19 (OPUS). THE SEMANTICS COME FROM ONE FUNCTION READ END TO END rather than from field shapes: 0051EF90(desc, src, count) loads capacity from +0x10 (0051EFAA) and used from +0x18 (0051EFB0), adds the count and compares (0051EFB4/0051EFB7), and when it does not fit reads the growth granularity from +0x14 (0051EFBC), computes ceil(count/granularity) by `lea eax,[rsi-1]; div r9d` (0051EFCB-0051EFD3), multiplies back (0051EFD6), forms `new capacity = old + that` (0051EFDD) and calls the reserve 0051EEB0. It then appends through the buffer pointer at +0x08 (0051EFE9) at the used offset (0051EFF2). THE CONSTRUCTOR'S ODD STORE IS EXPLAINED BY THAT: 0051EE12's `mov qword ptr [rcx+0x14], 0x800` is not a qword field - it writes BOTH dwords, setting the granularity to 0x800 and zeroing used in one instruction, which is why a naive reading would have declared a 64-bit field spanning +0x14..+0x1B. THE EXTENT IS CONFIRMED TWO WAYS, which is what makes this declarable where the skeleton is not: the census reaches +0x18 and no further at windows 0x20, 0x80 and 0x400, so the object ends at 0x1C - and 0x1C is exactly the span already allotted to it inside RenderResourceEntry, derived independently from that type's own adjacency. Two derivations, one number. NOT CLAIMED: that this is a store-wide utility. The five functions that take it (0051EE10, 0051EEB0, 0051EF90, 0051F020, 0051EE00, 006B5C70) have two to five callers each, so on present evidence it is private to this entry - the NAME says so even though the SHAPE is a perfectly generic dynamic array, and if it is later found elsewhere the rename is cheap. exe 73461d0896204b1c259c52f61aef4efbc95a2ffc388cadb36493d5d1d89721f8 || THE DECLARED EXTENT CANNOT BE A C `sizeof`, AND THIS IS NOT RESOLVED - 2026-09-20 (OPUS), from check_alignment.py (`size 0x1C, strictest align 8, remainder 4`). The type holds an 8-byte pointer at +0x008, so its alignment is 8 and any C `sizeof` for it must be a multiple of 8. 0x1C is not. TWO READINGS, AND NOTHING MEASURED CHOOSES BETWEEN THEM. (a) The type is really 0x20 with four bytes of TAIL PADDING, and the parent's `unobservedDword02C` at RenderResourceEntry +0x02C IS that padding - which would make the parent's layout natural, since 0x10 + 0x20 = 0x30 lands exactly on the 8-aligned `reference`. (b) The `size` column means the OCCUPIED SPAN rather than a sizeof, in which case 0x1C is right and the question is about the column's meaning rather than this type. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED. Reading (a) is tidy and would consume `unobservedDword02C`, an unexplained gap, purely to make the layout look complete - and nothing observed writes +0x2C. An extent is not evidence about the bytes past it. Recorded so a reconstruction knows it cannot emit this type as a plain C struct at 0x1C whichever reading holds: it must pad to 0x20 or inline the members into the parent. || TAIL-PADDING REPORT ADJUDICATED 2026-09-20 (OPUS). check_alignment reports size 0x1C as not a multiple of 8, which is this type's strictest alignment because of the void* at +0x08, remainder 4. THAT IS THE PARENT'S PADDING AND THE PARENT DECLARES IT: this type is EMBED RenderResourceEntry +0x10, the parent's own row for it is bufferDescriptor at +0x10 with a width of 28, and the next parent row is unobservedDword02C at +0x2C. So the four bytes the alignment rule wants are accounted for ONE LEVEL UP, where they belong - an embedded region's extent is the span between its neighbours, and inventing a tail pad here would take those four bytes from a row that already has them.

before.name: flagsByte2
before.meaning: flag byte. Its low nibble is CONSTRUCTION-FINAL: all six constructors memset the 0x890 template, and only two OR 0x0C into +0x002 - the type-2 EFB loader 0026FB90 (0026FC60) and the type-3 constructor 003B38B0 (003B3984); the type-1 (002FC4A0), type-4 (003B29B0), type-5 (003B0660) and type-7 (003B2220) constructors leave it zero and 0024B3A0 copies the byte verbatim into the heap context. Post-copy exactly two bodies write it, both the same nibble merge new = (old & 0x0F) | (entry+0x16 & 0xF0): 0026FD26 on a type-2 context and 003B22A0 on a type-7 context. So bits 0-3 never change after construction; bits 4-7 merge in from a slot record's +0x16
before.evidence: 003B3984 or byte ptr [rsp+0x22], 0xc BIT 2 (0x04) IDENTIFIED 2026-09-13 (ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-EFX-INPUT-LIFETIME): it means THIS CONTEXT IS PUBLISHED/SHARED, and it does two jobs that were verified separately before being joined. 003B348A test byte ptr [rcx+2],4 / je - 003B3480 publishes the context into the global 02F97340 and runs the rebase ONLY when the bit is set. 003A9613 test byte ptr [rax+2],4 / jne - the teardown 003A9600 (and its mirror 003A9950) SKIPS releasing the chunk at +0x870 / +0x878 when the bit is set, while still clearing the pointer. So the same bit that authorises publication withholds the free, which reads as deliberate: a shared context's chunk is owned elsewhere. OBJECT IDENTITY IS BY WRITE SITE, NOT BY OFFSET: 003B34B2 stores this very object into 02F97340 and the teardown reads that same global (all three RIP displacements resolved and compared). WRITER CENSUS CLOSED 2026-09-13 (OPUS-REQ-SWE2-STRUCT-EFXFLAG-WRITERS, SWE2-STRUCT): the complete writer set is {six constructor memsets -> 0; or 0x0C in 0026FB90 and 003B38B0 only; the 0024B3A0 bulk copy propagating the byte; the merges at 0026FD26 and 003B22A0}. Coverage: all six 0024B3A0 call sites enumerated twice - callgraph edges and a linear .text E8 sweep agree on 0026FC8A, 002FC54B, 003B073A, 003B2255, 003B2A6A, 003B39A4, and no indirect references to the copier exist; every referencer of 02F97340 (60 refs / 28 fns) and of the five interior-pointer globals 02EBEF70/78/90/A0/A8 covered by gptr-seeded hop_scan (214 accesses in 64 fns; positive controls FOUND - reader 003A9613 and known writer 0026FD26 both surfaced); all thirteen 020910A0 referencers hand-decoded (none stores +0x002; several walk the sibling 0x3B0 family whose links are +0x348/+0x350 on the +0x50 slots and which is published at 02F97348 by the 0024B270 copier - a different type, not a context); the 0024F610 list-finder callers, the publisher argument chains and all seven constructor callers hand-decoded; hop-8/hop-10 upper bounds (2436 and 1862 fns) audited and every additional disp-2 write verified a false propagation chain onto another record type (001AAF80 generic record copier, 00266530 ActorStorage, 0036B160 handle records, 0017C890 stream writer, 007F6FB0 buffer writer). VERDICT: the OR is NOT universal - exactly types 2 and 3 carry it - so bit 0x04 is set iff template type is 2 or 3, and the release at 003A9625 (mirror 003A9975) IS reachable: any type-1/4/5/7 context takes it when +0x003 bit 0 is latched and the run pointer is non-null, which is the designed path for the run-collected types 4 and 5. RESIDUAL LIMIT, stated not closed: a context stashed into an opaque object field (002FC550 caller+0x08, 003B2266 caller+0x08, 003B39A9 node+0x18) and read back by a body touching no seeded surface escapes this census; none is known. BIT 0x08 shares the same provenance - the 0x0C sets both bits - and is tested separately at 00500CBC and 00503E85; its distinct meaning is not claimed here.
